## Where is conflict concentrated, and how has it changed?

The study follows **330 Myanmar townships over 57 months**.

- Local Moran’s I identifies clusters and outliers.
- Gi* identifies hotspots and coldspots.
- Mann–Kendall and EHSA examine their changes through time.
- A separate comparison focuses on events targeting civilians.

::: {.small-note}
Sources: [ACLED Myanmar](https://acleddata.com/country/myanmar), supplied through eLearn; [MIMU v9.4](https://geonode.themimu.info/layers/geonode:mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1). Counts describe recorded events, not risk per person.
:::

## Preparing the township records

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.key-number}
53,805
:::

events retained from three categories: battles, explosions/remote violence and violence against civilians.
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
- The supplied file contains 87,109 records, including non-violent events.
- 107 relevant records lack a named township; another 88 have only a broad location.
- Months with no recorded event remain in the data.
- Three island townships have no Queen neighbours and remain unclassified in those tests.
:::
:::

## The monthly total peaks in late 2023

![](take-home-02/figures/monthly.png){height=430 alt="Monthly conflict counts by event type."}

January–September 2025 has **12.4% fewer events** than the same months of 2024. Explosions and remote violence remain the largest category.

## Clusters and outliers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="67%"}
![](take-home-02/figures/local-association.png){height=570 alt="Local Moran’s I and Gi-star results."}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
Gi* identifies **38 hotspots**:

- 18 in Sagaing;
- seven in Mandalay;
- six in Magway.

Local Moran’s I finds 38 high–high clusters, 52 low–low clusters and four low–high outliers.

::: {.small-note}
Queen neighbours; 999 permutations; p < 0.05. Grey means no significant result.
:::
:::
:::

## Following concentrations through time

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="67%"}
![](take-home-02/figures/ehsa.png){height=570 alt="Mann–Kendall trends and emerging hotspot patterns."}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
The full EHSA classification finds **26 oscillating** and **eight sporadic hotspots**.

Of these, 23 also have significant trends and appear here.

An area can have many earlier hot months without being a hotspot at the September 2025 endpoint.

::: {.small-note}
Current and preceding month; whole-cube Gi* reference. Map restricted to trend p < 0.05.
:::
:::
:::

## The civilian-targeting pattern

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="67%"}
![](take-home-02/figures/civilian-hotspots.png){height=570 alt="Gi-star maps for all retained records and the civilian-targeting subset."}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**16,391 events** in the retained data targeted civilians.

Their map has **37 hotspots**, with 34 overlapping the overall conflict hotspots.

Hakha, Tonzang and Nawnghkio appear only in the civilian-targeting hotspot map.

::: {.small-note}
These are events targeting civilians, not civilian deaths. The flag excludes incidental civilian harm.
:::
:::
:::

## How much confidence should we place in the maps?

- Adjusting for multiple tests reduces the overall Gi* hotspots from **38 to 19**.
- Gi* classifications agree in **87.2%** of townships under a different neighbour definition.
- Checking related months reduces significant trends from **`r sum(a$ehsa$trend_p < .05, na.rm=TRUE)` to `r sum(a$ehsa$block_p < .05, na.rm=TRUE)`**; **`r sum(a$ehsa$block_q < .05, na.rm=TRUE)`** remain after also adjusting for multiple tests.
- Kawkareik and Nawnghkio retain evidence of upward trends under the stronger checks.

Reporting gaps, approximate locations and different township sizes remain limitations. A low count or grey area does not establish safety.

## Recommended actions

- In **Sagaing, Mandalay and Magway**, compare hotspot townships with aid coverage and identify communities still waiting for food, shelter or medical support.
- In **Kawkareik and Nawnghkio**, ask local aid groups whether displacement has increased demand beyond what they can provide.
- In **Monywa**, check displaced households’ housing, food and healthcare needs before reducing any existing aid.
- In **Hakha, Tonzang and Nawnghkio**, review civilian-targeting incidents and neighbouring townships to locate the affected communities and check their needs.

Update the records beyond September 2025 and confirm current needs with local aid groups before acting.
